html:
A Portuguese navigator who led a Spanish fleet west to reach the Spice Islands. His expedition made the first voyage around the world, from 1519 to 1522, but he did not live to finish it.

Magellan had sailed to India and Malacca for Portugal. After a quarrel with King Manuel he took his plan to the young Spanish king, later the emperor Charles V: sail west, find a passage through the Americas, and reach the Moluccas, which he argued lay in Spain's half of the world.

He left Spain in September 1519 with five ships and about 270 men. In late 1520 he found the strait at the tip of South America that now bears his name. Crossing the Pacific took over three months, and many died of scurvy. In March 1521 he reached the Philippines, where he gave the Santo Niño to the converted rulers of Cebu. He was killed fighting Lapulapu's men on Mactan. Juan Sebastián Elcano brought one ship, the Victoria, back to Spain in 1522 with 18 men.
